---
title: "Discovering R Installations"
description: "Learn how Positron finds R installations on macOS, Windows, and Linux, and how to use settings to change which ones appear and which one starts."
---

This guide explains how Positron finds R installations and how to use settings to change which ones appear in the Interpreter picker and which one starts.
For using R in Positron, see our [R language guide](guide-r.qmd).

## R installation discovery

Positron consults various sources to build the list of available R interpreters:

* Well-known R root folders for the specific operating system:
  - macOS: `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions`
  - Linux: `/opt/R`
  - Windows: `%ProgramW6432%/R` (typically resolves to `C:/Program Files/R`) and
    `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Programs/R` (typically resolves to
    `C:/Users/username/AppData/Local/Programs/R`)

  These locations are treated as so-called root folders, meaning we expect them
  to contain one or more versions of R, not to actually be an R installation.
* The `PATH`, meaning the R executable that `which R` finds (except on Windows by default, as set by [`positron.r.interpreters.pathDiscoveryMode`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.pathDiscoveryMode))
* Well-known paths to an R executable or to a symlink that resolves to an R executable, e.g.:
  - `/usr/bin/R`
  - `/usr/local/bin/R`
  - `/opt/local/bin/R`
  - `/opt/homebrew/bin/R`
* R installations recorded in the Windows registry, in keys such as:
  - `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\R-core\R64\X.Y.Z`
  - `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\R-core\R64\X.Y.Z`
  where `X.Y.Z` is a concrete R version, such as 4.4.2.
  - It's often possible to discover which of those R versions is considered
    the current version of R from the registry keys
    `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\R-core\R64\InstallPath` or
    `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\R-core\R64\InstallPath`.

## Customizing R discovery

To open the settings in this section, run _Preferences: Open Settings_ from the Command Palette, then select **Extensions > R > Advanced**.
After you change any of these settings, restart Positron.

### Look in more places

If you have an R installation that won't be discovered by the search strategy described above, settings are available to instruct Positron to look in additional locations:

* [`positron.r.customRootFolders`](positron://settings/positron.r.customRootFolders): Suitable for R root folders that contain 1 or more R installations.
  - Hypothetical example: `C:/nonstandardRLocation`
* [`positron.r.customBinaries`](positron://settings/positron.r.customBinaries): Suitable for specific R executables.
  - Hypothetical example: `C:/nonstandardRLocation/R-4.4.1/bin/x64/R.exe`
* [`positron.r.interpreters.condaDiscovery`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.condaDiscovery): Enables discovery of R installations managed by conda. This support is experimental and not all Positron features may work as expected.
* [`positron.r.interpreters.pixiDiscovery`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.pixiDiscovery): Enables discovery of R installations managed by pixi. This support is also experimental.
* [`positron.r.interpreters.pathDiscoveryMode`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.pathDiscoveryMode): Controls whether Positron looks for the R on your `PATH`, which is the R that `which R` finds.
  - `auto` (the default): Looks on macOS and Linux, but not on Windows, where searching the `PATH` can be slow.
  - `on`: Always looks.
  - `off`: Never looks.

### Hide or limit R installations

To keep some R installations out of the Interpreter picker, use one of these settings.
Each setting takes a list of R executables or folders.

* [`positron.r.interpreters.exclude`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.exclude): Hides the R installations you list. A folder hides every R installation at or under that folder. This includes R installations that Positron finds through `positron.r.customRootFolders` or `positron.r.customBinaries`.
  - Example: `/opt/R/4.2.3` hides R 4.2.3 on Linux.
* [`positron.r.interpreters.override`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.override): Shows only the R installations you list. List R executables, or folders that hold R installations as subfolders, the way `/opt/R` holds `/opt/R/4.4.2` and `/opt/R/4.3.3`. If you list the folder of one installation, such as `/opt/R/4.4.2`, Positron finds nothing there. To show a single installation, list its R executable, such as `/opt/R/4.4.2/bin/R`.
  - Example: `/opt/R` shows only the R installations in `/opt/R`.

When you set `override`, Positron does not search anywhere else.
It skips all of these sources:

* The locations at the top of this page
* The `PATH`
* The Windows registry
* The `r-versions` file that Posit Workbench and RStudio Server use
* R installations from conda, pixi, and environment modules
* The `positron.r.customRootFolders` and `positron.r.customBinaries` settings in [Look in more places](#look-in-more-places)

Positron also ignores `exclude` when you set `override`.

### Choose which R starts

[`positron.r.interpreters.default`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.default) sets the R that Positron uses in a folder.
Set it to the path of one R executable that exists on disk, not a folder.

* Example on Linux: `/opt/R/4.4.2/bin/R`
* Example on macOS: `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.4-arm64/Resources/bin/R`
* Example on Windows: `C:/Program Files/R/R-4.4.2/bin/x64/R.exe`

Setting a default does not change which R your system treats as its current R version.

When you set a default, Positron uses that R every time it starts R in the folder, even if you used a different R there last time.
You can still start a different R from the Interpreter picker.
The next time you open the folder, Positron starts the default again.

Where you set the default decides which folders it applies to:

* In your user settings, it applies to every folder you open.
* In a project's `.vscode/settings.json` file, which holds the workspace settings, it applies only to that project. A value in a project's settings takes precedence over the value in your user settings.

`exclude` and `override` take precedence over the default.
If `exclude` hides the default, or `override` does not list it, Positron ignores the default.
If the default path does not exist, Positron ignores the default and chooses an R as if you had not set a default.

If you do not set a default, Positron remembers the R you use in each folder.
Once you start an R console in a folder, Positron uses that R there from then on.

There is one exception.
If the remembered R was the current R on your system at the time, Positron starts your current R instead.
For example, after you change your current R with `rig default`, that folder uses the R you switched to.

If `exclude` later hides the remembered R, or `override` leaves it out, Positron does not start it.
Instead, Positron chooses an R for that folder again.

To make a folder forget its R, run _Interpreter: Clear Saved Interpreter_ from the Command Palette.
This command does not stop a running R console.
If you keep using that console, Positron remembers its R again, so shut the console down first.

The [`interpreters.startupBehavior`](positron://settings/interpreters.startupBehavior) setting controls whether R starts on its own when you open a folder.
To learn more, see [Interpreter Startup](interpreter-startup.qmd).

### Use `${workspaceFolder}` in paths

These five settings accept `${workspaceFolder}` in their paths:

* `positron.r.customRootFolders`
* `positron.r.customBinaries`
* `positron.r.interpreters.exclude`
* `positron.r.interpreters.override`
* `positron.r.interpreters.default`

Positron replaces `${workspaceFolder}` with the path of the folder you have open.
This helps most in a project's `.vscode/settings.json` file, which you often share with your team.
Each person checks the project out to a different place, so a fixed absolute path does not work for everyone.
`${workspaceFolder}` makes the same path work for everyone.

For example, suppose a project keeps a conda environment with R in an `env` folder inside the project.
On macOS and Linux, set `positron.r.interpreters.default` to `${workspaceFolder}/env/bin/R`.
On Windows, the R in a conda environment is at `${workspaceFolder}/env/Lib/R/bin/x64/R.exe`.

The first four settings take a list of paths, and `positron.r.interpreters.default` takes a single path.
This example sets the project's default R on macOS and Linux:

```{.json filename=".vscode/settings.json"}
{
  "positron.r.interpreters.default": "${workspaceFolder}/env/bin/R"
}
```

Paths in these settings follow these rules:

* Use absolute paths. Positron ignores relative paths.
* You can start a path with `~` to mean your home folder.
* `${workspaceFolder}` is the only supported variable. Positron ignores a path that uses any other variable, such as `${HOME}`, `$HOME`, or the Windows form `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
* In a workspace with more than one folder, Positron uses the first folder for `${workspaceFolder}`.
* If no folder is open, Positron ignores any path that uses `${workspaceFolder}`.

## Unsupported R installations

Positron only supports R 4.2 and higher.
Older R versions might be discovered in the search described above, but they will be discarded.

On macOS, Positron only supports the system's current R version and other R installations that are orthogonal.

What does orthogonal mean here?
The `R` executable on macOS (and Linux) is actually a shell script that's responsible for launching R.
In an orthogonal R installation, this script targets the home of a specific, concrete version of R, such as `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.4-arm64`.
In a non-orthogonal R installation, this script targets the home of the current R version (literally, `/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources`, which is a symlink).
The CRAN installer leaves a non-orthogonal R installation behind and, by default, removes the previous version of R.

The notion of orthogonality comes from a tool called [rig: The R Installation Manager](https://github.com/r-lib/rig).
We highly recommend rig for managing R installation, especially for macOS users who want to have more than one functioning R installation.

## Troubleshooting

### R installation not appearing

If an R installation does not appear in the Interpreter picker, check these items in order:

1. Check that Positron supports that R version. See [Unsupported R installations](#unsupported-r-installations).
2. Check that `exclude` does not hide the installation. If you set `override`, check that it lists the installation. See [Hide or limit R installations](#hide-or-limit-r-installations).
3. Check that Positron looks in the location of that R installation. See [Look in more places](#look-in-more-places).
4. After you change any of the settings on this page, restart Positron.
5. Check the R Language Pack output channel.

The discovery process is logged in the R Language Pack channel.
You can learn more in the [troubleshooting guide](troubleshooting.qmd).
